sentences.text: The accused filed an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. in which an order was passed by the Madras High Court deleting Section 406 IPC as one of the charges.

Both the complainant as well as the accused filed their SLPs before this Court being SLP (Crl.) No.8803/2022 and SLP (Crl.) No.9500/2022 which were disposed of by a common order dated 03.07.2023 which reads as under:
Delay condoned in D. NO. 17598/2023.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
We are not inclined to exercise jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution of India.
The special leave petitions are dismissed.
We make it clear that since charge sheet has been filed, at the stage of framing of charges, the accused have always a right to urge for seeking discharge.

Mr. S.
Nagamuthu, learned senior counsel refers to the fact that main officers of the company are in Mumbai and if at all any offences have been committed, they are at the regional office at Chennai.

That being the position, that could be a matter to be urged before the trial Court and if exemption is sought for personal appearance, we are sure the trial Court will consider it appropriately so long as the trial is not impeded.

Needless to observe, at the insistence of the learned counsel for the parties,
that de hors the orders of the High Court, it will be open to the parties to urge for framing charges under Section 406 IPC and also for seeking discharge from the charges in respect of Section 420, IPC.
Pending applications stand disposed of.

Now an application for modification has been filed by the accused seeking deletion of the part of the order where it has been left open to the parties to urge for framing of charges under Section 406 IPC.
Heard learned Senior Advocates for the parties.

There is absolutely no doubt that although this Court did not interfere with the impugned order, however, it has left open to the parties to urge for framing of charges under Section 406 IPC at an appropriate stage.
We find absolutely no reason to interfere with this order.
I.A. No.155937/2023 is, accordingly, dismissed.
M.A. stands disposed of.

(KAVITA PAHUJA) (RENU BALA GAMBHIR)
